candidates.title: Find local news gaps across outlets

demandEvidence.chore: Building a tool to see what is yet not picked up by the outlets in your own country.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Building a tool to see what is yet not picked up by the outlets in your own country.

ease.reason: A manually supplied set of outlet headlines can be compared, but no supplied reference supports feed access or reliable story matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent local publishers or media researchers may pay for a coverage-gap brief; the post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare operator-supplied headlines; outlet coverage, language matching and live feeds remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can group possible matching stories, but a researcher must validate equivalence and decide what counts as local coverage.

evidence.reason: The post states a tool idea for finding stories not picked up by local outlets, but gives no workflow detail, frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: A dated list of supplied stories that may be missing from a selected local outlet, with source headlines for human review.
inputs: Operator-supplied headline and URL rows from several outlets
A selected country and outlet list
Synthetic story pairs with known matching labels
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator uploads a new batch of headline rows for one country.
steps: Normalize supplied headline text and outlet labels.
Group likely matching stories using proposed text similarity.
List stories without a likely match at the selected outlet.
Attach the supplied headlines and URLs to each possible gap.
Have a researcher confirm matches and coverage gaps.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a small synthetic batch with known duplicate and unmatched stories, compare every flagged gap with the expected labels and retain the supporting headline rows.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A researcher supplies permitted headline data, sets the matching threshold, verifies story equivalence and approves any published gap claim.
unverified: Reliable outlet feed access and reuse permission
A repeat buyer and willingness to pay

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposal from the assigned post; provisional mean 4.4. Below 6; recorded in rejected.

candidates.title: Flag possible repeat runs before processing

demandEvidence.chore: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.

ease.reason: The task is concrete, but no supplied implementation reference documents idempotency or trigger replay prevention.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow consultants or lead-generation operators may pay to reduce duplicate processing; this single post proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week replay simulation with synthetic event IDs is bounded; actual schedule recovery and matching keys remain unknown.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checker can compare supplied batch keys, but a person must define safe keys and change the workflow.

evidence.reason: One task span explicitly says missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything; frequency, affected records and mitigation are missing from these spans.

experimentPlan.output: A review report identifying records in a supplied batch that appear to have been processed before.
inputs: Operator-selected fields that identify a record
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a new sample batch for comparison with a saved synthetic prior-run list.
steps: Read the two supplied sample lists.
Compare records using operator-selected keys.
Mark exact and uncertain matches separately.
Show matched IDs and the selected comparison fields.
Ask an operator to validate flags before any workflow change.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use synthetic lists containing known repeats, new rows and ambiguous IDs; check that exact repeats are flagged and ambiguous rows are not silently discarded.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A workflow owner chooses identifiers, confirms whether records are truly duplicates and authorizes any production change.
unverified: Actual missed-trigger behavior and event identifiers
Whether deduplication keys are stable and unique
Any supported schedule or persistence integration

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposal from the assigned post; provisional mean 4.6. Below 6; recorded in rejected.

candidates.title: Pass received images into product inquiry review

demandEvidence.chore: I want the AI agent to recognize that the image has already been received and use the available image to identify the product, rather than asking the customer to resend it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want the AI agent to recognize that the image has already been received and use the available image to identify the product, rather than asking the customer to resend it.

ease.reason: A paired synthetic message and image can be assembled for review, but no supplied reference supports Make routing, Messenger access or image interpretation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service businesses handling product inquiries may pay to reduce avoidable repeat-image requests; the post proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can test whether supplied image references stay attached to messages; actual image access and identification quality are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can package supplied context, but a person must confirm the image and product match before replying.

evidence.reason: The retained post span describes text and image routes and an agent asking for an already received image; recurrence is not established in these spans.

experimentPlan.output: A review packet pairing each supplied customer message with its already supplied image reference and a proposed product description.
inputs: Operator-supplied test image or image placeholder
experimentPlan.trigger: A test message record includes text and a linked image reference.
steps: Read the supplied message and image reference together.
Check that both fields belong to the same synthetic message ID.
Draft a short product description for operator review.
Mark the image as unavailable when the reference is missing.
Have a person verify the description and approve any reply.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For paired and unpaired synthetic message records, confirm the packet retains the correct image reference and never claims an image was inspected when it was absent.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies permitted test inputs and verifies image interpretation; no live Messenger reply or purchase recommendation is sent automatically.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a bounded proposal from the assigned post; provisional mean 4.6. Below 6; recorded in rejected.

candidates.title: Review booking requests for possible conflicts

demandEvidence.chore: Preventing booking assistants from hallucinating relative dates or registering double-bookings
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Many AI booking assistants fail in production because LLMs can hallucinate relative dates (“next Friday”) or register double-bookings.

ease.reason: The spans describe a specific architecture using deterministic code and SQL checks, but no supplied building reference documents those capabilities for a student build.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent salon operators may pay for fewer booking conflicts; the post shares a maker architecture and establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic request-and-calendar simulation is bounded; salon-specific availability and production database access remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checker can flag conflicts in supplied test slots, while a person confirms availability and authorizes each booking.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe intent extraction and SQL slot validation in a maker-reported architecture; external use and corroboration are absent.

experimentPlan.output: A review queue of synthetic salon booking requests marked as apparently available, conflicting or unclear.
inputs: Synthetic booking request with date and time
Synthetic provider availability and existing appointments
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator adds a synthetic booking request to a test queue.
steps: Extract the requested date and time from the supplied test request.
Compare it with supplied hours and provider availability.
Check the synthetic appointment list for overlap.
Mark unclear or conflicting requests for review.
Require a person to confirm availability before any booking.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use synthetic requests covering an open slot, a closed hour, an existing overlap and an ambiguous date; verify each output against the supplied calendar rows.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A salon operator supplies and verifies hours and appointment records, resolves ambiguous dates and confirms all bookings; no live calendar or payment action is proposed.
unverified: Relevant n8n, PostgreSQL and calendar implementation support
Real calendar permissions and data reliability
Whether salons would pay for this proposed service

candidates.title: Review repeated Make data-sync failures

ease.reason: Make documentation (428eda549e557f199c3af452) documents routing an error to a configured handler; it does not document duplicate detection or repair.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small firms using business automations may pay for troubleshooting; this post offers a service but proves no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can classify operator-supplied error cases and draft next checks; live service access and deduplication remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed report can organize cases, but a person must diagnose root cause and authorize scenario edits; the error handler alone does not fix repeats.

evidence.reason: The retained post lists duplicate records and other recurring failure examples, but no single case, frequency or independent corroboration is supplied.

experimentPlan.output: A short review note for one supplied Make failure, separating observed symptoms from checks an operator could try.
inputs: Synthetic input and output record IDs
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one failed or repeated-data example for review.
steps: Record the expected and observed outcomes.
Check supplied IDs for exact repeated outputs.
Use Make error-handler documentation to explain that an error route can intercept module errors.
List missing facts needed to diagnose the issue.
Have a Make operator verify and authorize any change.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On synthetic examples with known duplicate IDs and a separate module error, verify that the note reports only visible symptoms and does not claim the handler prevents duplicates.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A Make operator supplies sanitized examples, diagnoses the actual scenario, tests changes and approves any production edits.
unverified: Access to and behavior of the actual Make scenario
Whether the example failures recur for paying customers
